[LCSP.3.5] **No intern-table lock.** `constspace` does not freeze the
string-intern table, and does not inherit the freeze `realtime` gets
([RTCT.12.4]). The lock is not a policy `constspace` declines — it has
nowhere to attach. Freezing needs a phase boundary after which no new
string may appear, and that boundary is `go_live`, which a
`constspace`-only engine never calls ([LCSP.6.5]).

What follows, stated plainly because it qualifies [LCSP.2.1]: a novel
string **arriving as a slot value on an asserted fact** interns at pump
time, and interning a string not already in the table may grow it. So
"no allocation on the hot path" holds for the pools [LCSP.2.1] names,
and does not hold for the intern table when the event trace carries
strings the DSC never saw.

An author who needs the stronger property takes `realtime`, where
`go_live` supplies the boundary and interning returns
`DS_ERR_OOM` rather than growing. A deployment that stays on
`constspace` bounds its string vocabulary by what it asserts —
which is an integrator obligation, not something the compiler checks.

[LNLS.3.2] is unaffected and still applies: it is a compile-time check
on strings a **rule produces** (an interpolated string), which is a
different population from strings a fact carries in.
